+## 18. Direction Control
+
+Before work in an active direction, run `node scripts/directions/root-loader.mjs <absolute-target-path>` from the registered owning worktree. The loader selects the owning manifest by its actual Git branch/common and returns the root, owning direction and applicable nested `AGENTS.md` contracts. Read every returned contract in order. A blocked result stops the affected work.
+
+The loader's scope result is read-only rule selection. It does not grant product mutation, adoption, publication, Verify, POST, archive or integration permission. The approved stage scope, root rules, applicable nested rules and current gates remain mandatory. A nested rule can add constraints but cannot waive a parent constraint. Textual tokens alone do not establish semantic equivalence.
+
+W01 owns only the approved engineering control and documentation paths. Routing, UI and Repository Core adoption remains separate in their owning workspaces. Do not use W01 metadata to authorize foreign product or direction changes.

+# Start or continue a Frade direction
+
+Status: W01 controls are `NOT_DEPLOYED_W01_CLOSURE_PENDING`; use the owning checkout and its current approved gates. Node 24.x, pnpm 12.6.0 and Git are the product toolchain. The pinned common review runtime is separate.
+
+Tell the agent: **“Открой направление <название>: <проблема>, <кому нужно>, <ожидаемый результат>, <ограничения>.”** The agent inventories owners, baseline, rules, affected contracts and acceptance, then proposes a bounded direction, exact stage roles and publication destination. You decide material goal/spec/scope, model, visual or destination questions when presented with concrete options. Do not move another owner's uncommitted work to start quickly.
+
+Read the current status decision and next step first, then scope, roadmap, tasks, required checks, approvals and publication. Run `node scripts/directions/root-loader.mjs <absolute-target-path>` in the registered owner to see root and applicable direction/nested rules. A blocked result means the affected task needs correction. The result is rule context only; use existing lifecycle, review, scope and closure commands for executor admission and stage gates.
+
+The available direction CLI commands are `plan`, `create`, `check`, `status`, `review/prepare`, `review`, `checkpoint` and `publish` through `node scripts/directions/cli.mjs`. Use the command's absolute JSON request or manifest path. The loader is a separate read-only command. Writer dispatch is `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; do not describe review transport as writer execution. Current model backend is `NOT_CONFIRMED` unless actual runtime provenance confirms it.
+
+From the registered owner, run `node scripts/directions/cli.mjs check <absolute-owned-direction.json>` before `node scripts/directions/cli.mjs status <absolute-owned-direction.json>`. After checking the preview and confirming no review freeze, `node scripts/directions/cli.mjs status <absolute-owned-direction.json> --write` refreshes the tracked projection and retains a prior manual status as history. The currently installed public review command admits only W01's approved packet: `node scripts/directions/cli.mjs review/prepare <absolute-W01-direction.json> POST <absolute-external-review-request.json>` checks it without dispatch; `review` with the same arguments performs the actual independent dispatch only when admitted. Other directions require their own reviewed admission. For publication, `checkpoint` takes the absolute manifest and a separate absolute event JSON; `publish` takes the resulting absolute checkpoint receipt JSON. Exact owner, source, check, approval and remote bindings remain required. The original W01 owner is admitted through its fixed historical evidence when bootstrap journals are absent; unrelated older owners still require reviewed adoption. A status count or generated header does not grant Verify, POST, archive or deployment.
+
+For continuation say: **“Продолжи направление <ID> с текущего checkpoint; проверь owner, baseline, rules, applicability and gates.”** Work follows planning and current PRE, meaningful RED, implementation, applicable checks, Verify, POST, archive and STOP. For a failure request the first failing invariant, reproduction, root cause and next allowed step. Keep prior failure evidence. Never update visual baselines as a normal verification step.
+
+The root `pnpm check` runs existing general product checks; `pnpm check:all` additionally runs browser and desktop tests. Their names do not prove execution. `pnpm check:directions` runs direction controls and W01 applicability proof in the actual owner checkout. Required OpenSpec and owner checks are recorded separately. CI definitions or branch protection remain `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_CONFIGURED` until observed remotely.
+
+An approved feature ref may receive tested task or significant checkpoint commits. Checkpoint and publish return distinct local and verified remote states. A published feature is not merged. For integration, ask for a candidate against an exact target SHA, conflict review and checks on the merged tree; merge awaits separate authorization. Routing, UI and Repo Core adoption remains `NOT_STARTED` until their owners perform it.

+# Frade direction workflow
+
+Status: `NOT_DEPLOYED_W01_CLOSURE_PENDING`. This text instantiates the accepted W01 design for engineering use. W01 checks, Verify, POST and closure still require actual evidence. Common review release v1.1 remains immutable. Writer dispatch is `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.
+
+A direction is an owned objective with one immutable original baseline, registered `codex/<id>` branch/worktree, approved scope and exact remote/ref. Stages contain tasks and ordered steps; legacy R/P stage IDs and history remain intact. Phase, health, applicability, publication and adoption are separate facts.
+
+The phase order is `INTAKE → RESEARCH → REQUIREMENTS → PLANNING → PRE_REVIEW → BDD_TDD → IMPLEMENTATION → CHECKS → VERIFICATION → POST_REVIEW → ARCHIVE → CLOSED`. A small feature can use one stage, with the same barriers. The agent inventories the repository and exact owner first, prepares proposal/spec/design/tasks and a check plan, obtains required material decisions, then performs current independent PRE, deterministic RED, scoped implementation and actual applicable checks. Formal Verify and current independent POST follow checks; only then may the owner consider exact sync/archive. Starting the next numbered direction or integrating into main requires its own authorization.
+
+The registered owner manifest lives at `docs/engineering/directions/<id>/direction.json`. The root loader selects it from the real Git branch/common and target path. Its rule result includes root, owning direction and path nested `AGENTS.md` contracts. Every contract remains in force; the loader does not interpret prose as equivalent and does not grant writes. Existing root sections 1–17, Routing V2 contracts and other applicable product contracts remain mandatory. Existing lifecycle, scope, review and closure controls make separate executor admission decisions; a loader result never substitutes for those current gates. A future closure flag causes the loader to report `CLOSURE_ADMISSION_NOT_EVALUATED`, leaving the actual closure decision to those controls.
+
+For every stage, declare required general and subsystem checks before execution. Record command, exit, source/config/environment, raw evidence and accepted limit. `REQUIRED` failures and unavailable checks block closure. `NOT_APPLICABLE` needs a contract reason and unchanged affected tree proof before execution; an applicable failure cannot become N/A. Process-only W01 runs direction controls, strict OpenSpec validation, root lint/type/build/boundary checks and content/hash/link/frozen audit. Product `check:all` remains `NOT_RUN` until executed; no product GREEN is inferred from control checks.
+
+The approved task or role assignment resolves to exactly one model and effort. Provenance records approved assignment, invoked pair and confirmed backend, or `NOT_CONFIRMED`. Reviewer PASS requires its independent confined transport; an owner or writer cannot self-approve. Shared writer dispatch remains unavailable.
+
+Keep an eight-block status in this order: decision/next step; identity/scope; roadmap; active tasks/steps; checks/gates/quality; models/execution; dependencies/decisions/blockers; Git/publication/evidence. Task counts are administrative progress. Keep historical FAIL and immutable receipts. After a tested task or significant checkpoint, publish only to the previously authorized feature ref using the checkpoint protocol and verify fresh remote SHA. A blocker checkpoint is labeled incomplete. Neither publication nor a completed checklist grants Verify, POST, closure, consumer adoption or main merge.
+
+Routing, UI and Repo Core adopt separately in their own worktrees, preserving origins and frozen contracts. A completed legacy checklist without formal closure is `IMPLEMENTED_PENDING_CLOSURE`. Main integration revalidates the actual merged candidate and needs its own permission.

+# Direction core contract v2
+
+This is the installable data and guard contract for task 2.1. It is a library, not a command dispatcher or a gate receipt. The planning draft manifest contains explanatory scope strings; an installed manifest uses only canonical repository paths and explicit closure fields as shown in `direction-manifest.v2.json`. The example's zero hashes and baseline are synthetic and grant no authority.
+
+## API and data
+
+`scripts/directions/contracts.mjs` exports `validateManifest(manifest)`, `scopeFingerprint(manifest)`, `validateTraceability(trace, options)`, `verifyTraceability(trace, {boundary,snapshot})`, `validateApplicability(plan)`, `verifyApplicability(plan, {boundary,snapshot})`, `safeId`, `safeRepoPath`, `safeOwnerPath`, `pathMatches`, and the exact phase, health, applicability enums. Validators return `{ok, issues}` with stable `{code,path,detail}` entries. Structural `ok` does not prove that Git ownership, a run, a review, or a human decision happened. The two asynchronous verify functions require current raw run evidence through the trusted boundary. Version 2 is the only accepted manifest version. Unknown versions fail closed.
+
+Direction IDs and stage IDs are stable. Owner branch is `codex/<id>` and the Windows worktree/common paths are canonical absolute paths. Repository paths use `/`, no traversal, link escape, alternate data stream, control character, `.git` segment, device name or uncontrolled wildcard. Real Git registration, case collisions and reparse points must also be checked by the future bootstrap or executor before a write. The manifest has distinct `scope.planningAllowed`, `scope.allowed`, `scope.frozen` and `scope.closure`; closure paths never enter routine `allowed`. W01's three exact spec destinations and owner-bound archive pattern are fixed by design. The archive date is a real canonical UTC `YYYY-MM-DD` chosen at execution.
+
+`scopeFingerprint` hashes only semantic scope: owner, baseline, policy, path sets, closure destinations, stage dependencies, role authority and task acceptance links. Phase, health, checkbox completion, admission display strings, checkpoint and metrics are progress fields. They do not change this fingerprint. Any semantic change requires coherent revalidation and a new approval/review binding. The raw approved plan SHA256 remains separate. PRE binds the reviewed plan and scope fingerprint; approved implementation source changes do not stale PRE. GREEN, checks, Verify and POST bind the current source and config hashes. POST also binds plan and scope.
+
+The trace contract has `requirements`, `scenarios`, `tasks`, `assertions` and `runs` arrays. Stable requirement IDs link to scenarios, reciprocal task links, assertion IDs and run IDs. Critical requirements require positive, negative and boundary controls. A scenario classified `human` or `future` needs a concrete `boundaryReason`; it is never executable acceptance. Unresolved acceptance blocks dependent implementation while research can continue. Run rows require source/config SHA256 and environment and retain FAIL/BLOCKED records. `verifyTraceability` checks current referenced PASS runs against trusted raw proof; older unreferenced FAIL rows remain in the history. Approved numeric limits remain in the owning contract and must not be changed to match a failure.
+
+The applicability contract has `checks` with `REQUIRED` or `NOT_APPLICABLE`, affected contracts and previous results. An affected or currently failing check cannot become N/A, and N/A needs a concrete contract reason. A required NOT_RUN/FAIL/BLOCKED check stays nonpassing. `verifyApplicability` requires trusted current proof for each required PASS. The verifier supplying check proof must compare the declared plan with actual commands, config, source, environment and raw run output. Scoped AGENTS and subsystem rules remain mandatory; this library cannot semantically waive them.
+
+## Evidence boundary
+
+`scripts/directions/evidence.mjs` exports `createArtifactReader(root)`, `verifyArtifactHash(reader, descriptor)` and `createEvidenceBoundary({verify})`. The reader checks relative paths, symlinks and canonical containment and returns raw bytes and SHA256. The trusted `verify` callback is an integration boundary, not a JSON parser: it must read and hash actual artifacts, compare source/config/run bindings, and for independent reviews check complete raw events, exit, report, candidate/packet/control/plan hashes, one unambiguous verdict, scope and currentness using the verified transport receipt. It must verify human policy decisions and owner checkpoints from their own authority. The caller must not construct a verifier that returns true from a manifest `PASS`, a boolean, or request metadata. No verifier is supplied by default. The later review wrapper and Git controls own those checks; this task does not claim they exist.
+
+A gate reference contains `kind`, `status: "PASS"`, `scope: "full"`, `complete: true`, `artifact: {path,sha256}` and `bindings`. These fields are necessary descriptors and never sufficient approval. `evaluateTransition` additionally requires a genuine boundary created with `createEvidenceBoundary`; a copied JSON object or object with a `verify` method is not one. A trusted callback may return true only after its raw proof checks. Missing, stale, malformed, focused or unverified proof returns a specific `*_PROOF` issue. Actual backend/effort remains `NOT_CONFIRMED` without separate attestation.
+
+`scripts/directions/lifecycle.mjs` exports `evaluateTransition({manifest,stageId,target,evidence,boundary,snapshot})` and conservative `legacyClosureState(record)`. Only the next phase is admissible. A FAIL/BLOCKED/PAUSED owner stops. `snapshot` supplies current plan, scope, source and config SHA256. PRE plus policy decision and owner checkpoint are required before BDD/TDD and implementation; RED before implementation; current GREEN/checks/Verify before POST; current independent POST before archive. A diagnostic PASS never replaces full approval. `legacyClosureState` maps completed old checkboxes to `IMPLEMENTED_PENDING_CLOSURE` even if historical text says PASS; only an actual verified closure operation may establish CLOSED.
+
+`scripts/directions/scope.mjs` exports `checkScope(manifest,phase,paths)`, `planClosure(args)` and the bounded `executeClosure(args)`. `checkScope` checks planning or implementation relative paths against frozen and allowed sets and always rejects closure paths. `planClosure` is a read-only proposed operation list after verified archive barriers. It requires exactly the declared delta spec syncs, one move of the selected owning active change to the exact dated archive, and explicit owned/immutable-origin mappings with raw hashes. Each relocated path retains its suffix under the archive root. With `reader: createArtifactReader(root)`, it also verifies each delta source's `sourceSha256` and each reference origin's SHA256 against actual bytes. Without a reader, a successful plan validates only path structure and gate references and is not ready for filesystem mutation. `executeClosure` performs the further Git and filesystem checks described below before writing only in disposable test repositories. This task does not perform W01 sync or archive.
+
+## Stable issue groups
+
+Schema/identity: `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `DIRECTION_ID`, `OWNER_BRANCH`, `OWNER_PATH`, `UNSAFE_PATH`, `FROZEN_OVERLAP`. Scope/closure: `SCOPE_DENIED`, `CLOSURE_INACTIVE`, `CLOSURE_DESTINATION`, `ARCHIVE_DATE`, `ARCHIVE_DESTINATION`, `REFERENCE_RELOCATION`. Lifecycle/evidence: `PHASE_ORDER`, `HEALTH_STOP`, `SCOPE_DRIFT`, `EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY`, `PRE_PROOF`, `GREEN_PROOF`, `VERIFY_PROOF`, `POST_PROOF`. Trace/applicability: `UNRESOLVED_ACCEPTANCE`, `TRACE_TASK`, `TRACE_ASSERTION`, `TRACE_RUN`, `CONTROL_NEGATIVE`, `CONTROL_BOUNDARY`, `FALSE_NOT_APPLICABLE`, `REQUIRED_CHECK_NOT_PASS`. Other issue codes follow the same `{code,path,detail}` shape.
+
+## Task 2.1 repair and schema migration
+
+Version 2 remains the manifest schema. Its `stages[].change` is an explicit, safe, unique mapping to an OpenSpec change within `scope.planningAllowed`; the direction ID continues to identify the branch. A multi-stage direction can therefore own independent numbered changes. `scope.closure.archiveOwner` selects an owned stage change for one bounded closure. W01 keeps its three exact capability spec destinations. Other directions may declare only `openspec/specs/<safe-capability>/spec.md`, never a product or frozen path. Paths reject Windows-invalid characters and case-fold conservatively for scope and frozen checks. Generic stable requirement IDs such as `DRAW-CORE-12` are accepted alongside `FWE-004`.
+
+The `evaluateTransition` API now checks `stage.failedFixes` for two deterministic FAIL outcomes of one defect. Another implementation transition requires `stage.rca` with one root AGENTS classification, concrete root and layer, and current trusted `evidence.rca` proof. `CLOSED` requires the actual closure receipt plus trusted `evidence.archive` proof bound to the operation digest, owner, current source/scope and archive HEAD. A PASS string or raw JSON boolean cannot supply either proof. `createEvidenceBoundary` remains an explicitly trusted integration adapter; task 2.5 owns actual review-protocol verification.
+
+`scope.mjs` also exports `executeClosure(args)` and `isClosureReceipt`. The executor is deliberately limited to isolated temporary Git roots named `frade-closure-*`, with no remote, a clean tree, exact owning branch, current HEAD and ancestor original baseline. It rechecks gate proofs, declared operations, all owner files and raw hashes, destination contents, links, case collisions and symlink safety before writes. It merges only exact delta requirement sections into exact capability spec files, preserves unrelated requirements, moves only the owning change, relocates owned relative links and role-source paths through an explicit origin map, and preserves immutable raw files and origin hashes. The actual W01 archive still belongs to its later Verify/POST/closure sequence. The original tests-only historical RED snapshot remains distinct from the later controlled behaviorless skeleton replay under `deliverables/repair-red`.

+# Exact role resolver contract (task 2.2)
+
+`scripts/directions/roles.mjs` exports `createRoleAuthority`, `resolveRole`, and
+`writableWorkerDispatch`. This document defines a reusable schema. Any example row in a
+template is **PROPOSED**, and cannot authorize dispatch. An approved plan and direct human
+or reviewed-plan authority must be established for each direction.
+
+## Inputs and authority
+
+`resolveRole({manifest, stageId, taskId, taskType, role, reader, authority, invoked, executionKind})`
+selects one exact stage/type/role assignment. A stage has `roleAssignments`, `roleAuthority`,
+and `taskOverrides` arrays. Each assignment has `role`, `model`, `effort`, and optional
+`taskType`, `executionKind`, and `source`. If `taskType` is absent, it equals `role`,
+as in approved W01. A supplied `executionKind` must agree with the distinct reviewer
+roles (`independent-PRE`, `independent-POST`, `reviewer`) or executor roles.
+`roleAuthority` or a row's `source` has canonical relative `path`, raw `sha256` (legacy
+draft `hash` accepted), `revision`, and a separate `decision: {path,sha256}`. The row's
+`source.excerpt`, when supplied, is the exact stage/type/role/pair table line in the raw
+source. The W01 table line is derived from the selected pair and checked for unique
+exact presence.
+
+The trusted controller chooses the artifact root for `createArtifactReader(root)` and
+creates `createRoleAuthority({bindings,verifyApproval})`. Bindings anchor source and
+decision paths, raw SHA256 values, and revisions independently of request or manifest
+metadata. The verifier must establish the direct human decision or reviewed approved
+plan from actual raw decision evidence and compare its scope, stage, task/type/role, pair,
+revision, and approval to the selected assignment. It must return `true` only after those
+checks. There is no default verifier. A JSON `PASS`, request pair, or manifest boolean is
+never approval. The resolver rereads raw source and decision bytes through the safe
+artifact reader, rejects hash drift, and requires one exact excerpt line. A trusted
+controller must keep its bindings and verifier outside writable request data.
+
+For W01, the accepted design binding is
+`openspec/changes/frade-standard-workflow/design.md` at
+`501168ced50a35e128a0fc86e79bab6ac9aa31cd343eca3eedac56f81570978a`.
+The direct decision binding is
+`openspec/changes/frade-standard-workflow/evidence/user-decisions.json` at
+`126589d990e2e44b04efe8825b5ec4d90582205ba6c729375528c383ccbaf186`.
+Revision `D03` binds the accepted concrete plan while the earlier model reply remains
+the exact model authorization. The five W01 rows are planning-architecture Astra/high,
+independent-PRE Astra/xhigh, tooling-tests Sol/high, formal-Verify Astra/high, and
+independent-POST Astra/xhigh. These values are W01 only.
+
+## Task exceptions and result
+
+A task exception has `taskId`, `taskType`, `role`, exact `model` and `effort`, nonempty
+`reason`, `source: {path,sha256,revision,excerpt}`, and
+`approval: {path,sha256}`. Its exact source row is
+`| <stage> | <task> | <type> | <role> | <model> | <effort> | exception: <reason> |`.
+The controller must verify the exception's own approval. It changes only the matching
+task and role; other tasks use their stage row. Missing, duplicate, contradictory,
+range, unapproved, forged, or drifted assignments return `{ok:false,status:'BLOCKED',issues}`.
+
+Successful resolution returns `{ok:true,status:'RESOLVED',assignment,provenance}`.
+`assignment` records stage, task, type, role, executor/reviewer kind, exact pair,
+source path/raw hash/excerpt/revision, and any exception reason and approval.
+`provenance.requested` is the selected approved pair; `provenance.invoked` is the
+optional caller-reported invocation and must match it exactly. Neither field attests
+the running model. `actualBackend`, `actualEffort`, and model availability remain
+`NOT_CONFIRMED` until separate runtime evidence exists. Unknown availability is a
+dispatch limitation and never licenses a model substitute.
+
+`writableWorkerDispatch()` always returns `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` / `BLOCKED`. It performs no
+launch, cannot switch the current chat, and cannot reuse the existing read-only
+independent reviewer packet as writable executor confinement. A future writable-worker
+integration needs separate owner-scope and runtime proof. Independent review transport
+and its confinement remain under their existing separate control.

+# Direction bootstrap (task 2.3)
+
+Use the actual current shared release in the canonical Frade Git common directory. The CLI resolves that common from its running control location before inspecting a requested source. It reads `frade-workflow/current.json`, checks the immutable release bundle and exact public policy bytes, and requires the existing runner's `status` to report `AVAILABLE` for that release. A missing, drifted or unavailable installation reports `BLOCKED`/`NOT_CONFIGURED`; the unfinished W01 implementation is not a deployed release. The request cannot select or assert its own control installation. Library tests pass an explicit branded, hash-verified fixture context.
+
+`plan` accepts a registered primary or secondary worktree from the same common. `create` additionally verifies the selected policy bytes in the committed baseline and current source checkout. The branch is created only after a matching actual registration, baseline ancestry, path and collision inspection. Availability of the installed review service does not authorize a direction. Before any intent journal or worktree write, `create` requires an external request grant at `<canonical Git common>/frade-workflow/bootstrap-authority.json`. The grant is a regular, canonical file written by a controller outside the requester. Production CLI commands never create or approve it. The fixture context replaces only service availability attestation; fixtures use the same grant verifier.
+
+The grant has `schemaVersion: 1`, canonical `sourceRoot`, `gitCommon`, approved `workspaceParent`, `baseline`, exact `policy`, and `intentHash`. The hash is SHA256 of the normalized request JSON serialized with `JSON.stringify` (Windows path separators normalize to `/` at the request boundary). The grant must match the requested registered source, Git common, parent, baseline, policy and exact intent hash. A different ID, title, goal, outcomes, destination or other request content needs a separate grant. A request field such as `approved: true` is invalid. The `plan` output's `authorityPath` identifies the external grant location; it grants no authority by itself.
+
+Create an absolute-path JSON request with these fields:
+
+```json
+{
+  "schemaVersion": 1,
+  "id": "example-direction",
+  "title": "Example direction",
+  "goal": "Describe the bounded goal",
+  "users": ["intended users"],
+  "outcomes": ["observable result"],
+  "constraints": ["preserve existing behavior"],
+  "exclusions": ["unrelated product files"],
+  "sourceRoot": "/absolute/canonical/frade",
+  "gitCommon": "/absolute/canonical/frade/.git",
+  "workspaceParent": "/absolute/canonical/owners",
+  "baseline": "40-lowercase-hex-committed-baseline",
+  "policy": {
+    "version": "reviewed-release-version",
+    "release": "64-lowercase-hex-release-id",
+    "sha256": "64-lowercase-hex-policy-hash",
+    "artifact": "policy/agent-workflow.md"
+  },
+  "publication": {
+    "remote": "git@example.test:team/frade.git",
+    "ref": "refs/heads/codex/example-direction",
+    "authorization": "pending human decision"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+From a registered source worktree:
+
+```sh
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs plan /absolute/path/request.json
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs create /absolute/path/request.json
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs check /absolute/canonical/owners/example-direction/docs/engineering/directions/example-direction/direction.json
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs status /absolute/canonical/owners/example-direction/docs/engineering/directions/example-direction/direction.json
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs status /absolute/canonical/owners/example-direction/docs/engineering/directions/example-direction/direction.json --write
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs checkpoint /absolute/canonical/owners/example-direction/docs/engineering/directions/example-direction/direction.json /absolute/path/checkpoint-event.json
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs publish /absolute/path/checkpoint-receipt.json
+```
+
+The currently installed public review preflight is bound to the registered W01 owner and its approved packet. From that owner, use `node scripts/directions/cli.mjs review/prepare E:/dev/codex/frade-worktrees/frade-standard-workflow/docs/engineering/directions/frade-standard-workflow/direction.json POST /absolute/path/review-request.json`. A generic new direction needs its own reviewed admission before that review command can succeed.
+
+`plan` returns a read-only JSON preview with exact branch, worktree, seed paths, committed baseline, policy, publication destination, unknowns, intent path and an intent hash. `create` returns JSON exit 0 only after the branch is registered and seed files exist; blocked JSON uses exit 2. The branch is `codex/<id>` and the manifest is branch-local. The seed preserves inherited root rules, marks model assignment and downstream gates unresolved, and creates no product package. The seed delta capability matches `openspec/specs/<id>/spec.md`; its draft contains a strict-valid SHALL requirement while product acceptance stays unresolved and blocking.
+
+The partial recovery protocol writes `<Git common>/frade-workflow/intents/<id>.json` with exclusive creation before `git worktree add`. It records the normalized request and its hash, branch, target, source, common, parent, baseline and policy. Every Git call uses command-local hook, fsmonitor and autocrlf settings. Checkout fails closed when committed or common info attributes request a smudge filter; no foreign filter code is run. The CLI verifies actual Git registration and baseline before seeding. A separate `<id>.complete.json` receipt with the exact same origin is written after seed files. A retry with the same granted request either finishes the retained work or returns the existing registered owner; it never cleans, resets or deletes an uncertain target. A different request, existing foreign branch/target, changed policy, unregistered target or case collision blocks without overwriting it. A partial failure returns `BLOCKED` and retains its intent and any registered worktree for inspection.
+
+`check` first confines the path to a registered worktree's exact owned direction manifest, before reading JSON. It then validates canonical parents, the v2 manifest, current selected policy bytes, actual Git owner and the exact original baseline in both retained origin records. It recomputes the normalized request hash and checks owner, source, parent and policy bindings. Ancestor status alone cannot establish the original baseline. The original W01 owner has a narrow historical exception authenticated by its fixed owner/common, original baseline, approved checkpoint and raw design, decision, audit, PRE and policy evidence; no bootstrap journals are fabricated. Other older owners without retained origin records remain `BLOCKED` pending reviewed legacy adoption. `check` grants no gate acceptance.
+
+`status` previews a source-bound projection; `--write` refreshes the tracked status only after owner and origin admission and outside a review freeze. The first generated projection preserves the existing manual status as historical text. `review/prepare` checks the request and installed approval provenance without dispatch; `review` invokes the confined independent reviewer only after its gates. `checkpoint` needs a separate authorized event file and actual checks; `publish` needs an authorized checkpoint receipt and verifies the exact remote SHA. These commands can return `BLOCKED` when the owner lacks the required reviewed admission; their presence is not approval. See the task 2.5 and 2.6 templates for their full command contracts. Writer dispatch remains `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. Safe research and decision recording can continue while acceptance cases, numeric limits, exact role assignments or publication authorization remain unresolved; dependent implementation and publication stay blocked.

+# Direction status contract (task 2.4)
+
+`node scripts/directions/cli.mjs status <absolute-manifest>` returns a JSON preview. Add `--write` to refresh the manifest's owned `statusPath`. The CLI checks the installed control, actual registered owner/branch/common, immutable bootstrap origin, tracked manifest, baseline ancestry and scope before writing. An uninstalled W01 manifest is not an active owner. The writable target is the direction's own `docs/engineering/directions/<id>/DIRECTION-STATUS.md`, or the existing W01 `docs/engineering/BRANCH-STATUS.md` with its registered origin. An in-scope control, spec, source or ordinary document cannot become the dashboard by changing `statusPath`.
+
+The projection uses the same eight Russian primary headings as the approved status template. `parseStatus` requires exactly one of each in order. `parseTasks` counts only checklist entries with stable numeric IDs and rejects duplicate or malformed entries. Administrative task counts never establish product acceptance. Requirements count as accepted only when all linked executable scenarios have current positive, negative and boundary assertion runs verified through a trusted evidence boundary. Human and future scenarios remain pending. The boundary must read the raw artifact bytes from the registered owner, hash them, check complete execution and assertion IDs, and bind source/config/environment to the current snapshot. `createArtifactReader` supplies confined, reparse-safe raw bytes. A `PASS` string, `verified: true`, or a path/hash declared in JSON is insufficient.
+
+The CLI deliberately supplies no evidence boundary. It reports unsupported proof as `NOT_VERIFIED` and leaves readiness blocked. An integration controller can call `projectStatus({ manifest, tasksText, trace, snapshot, checks, boundary, updatedAt })` with an independently trusted `createEvidenceBoundary({ verify })`. `verify` receives `(kind, ref, expected)` and must validate raw run/check artifacts and current bindings. A `check` ref uses the same complete/full/PASS/artifact/bindings shape as a `run` ref. Approved numeric limits must be supplied by a future verified contract source; arbitrary check fields do not change the limit or earn a quality score. PRE, Verify, POST, publication and human visual decisions remain separate gates.
+
+The status projection and bootstrap seed report `PANEL_STATE: NOT_OPENED` until a trusted external UI controller supplies an actual `QUEUED` or `VISIBLE` operation receipt. The controller passes `panelBoundary` from `createPanelControllerBoundary({ verify })` and `panelReceipt` to `projectStatus` or `refreshStatus`. Its verifier must read the raw receipt bytes, hash them and bind the operation state, registered owner and status path. Request JSON fields such as `panelState` or `verified` cannot attest an operation. A CLI write cannot open the panel or assert visibility. This follows FWE-015's distinction between queued opening and confirmed visibility and shared AGENTS §20's rule that queued is not proof of visibility.
+
+The status source input SHA256 binds the manifest, checklist text, trace records, snapshot and checks. For a registered-owner refresh it also binds the actual Git HEAD checkpoint. A preview identifies a previous projection with different source input as `STALE_PROJECTION`. A refresh keeps an existing historical tail byte for byte after `<!-- LEGACY HISTORY: historical only -->`; an older dashboard without the current headings is moved verbatim below that boundary. Historical FAIL remains historical and visible.
+
+The freeze marker is `<canonical Git common>/frade-workflow/freeze/<direction-id>.json`. A present regular marker defers dashboard writes; a link or malformed location blocks. The status engine rechecks its canonical parents and marker immediately before writing, including after awaited evidence verification. The later review wrapper owns marker creation/removal and serial coordination with refresh. This status CLI neither opens the Codex panel nor changes the index/HEAD, creates a commit, pushes, reviews, or approves a gate. Checkpoint and remote SHA fields require later publication receipt integration; they show `NOT_VERIFIED` until then.
+
+For a registered, tracked owner after bootstrap checkpoint:
+
+```sh
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs status /absolute/owner/docs/engineering/directions/example-direction/direction.json
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs status /absolute/owner/docs/engineering/directions/example-direction/direction.json --write
+```

+# W01 task 2.5 review adapter
+
+The adapter in `scripts/directions/review.mjs` consumes the installed, immutable Frade v1.1 shared runner. It does not change its transport or publish a new shared release. The public CLI currently admits only the registered W01 owner in the canonical Frade Git common directory:
+
+```text
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs review/prepare <absolute-installed-manifest> PRE|POST <absolute-external-request.json>
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs review <absolute-installed-manifest> PRE|POST <absolute-external-request.json>
+```
+
+`review/prepare` is a structural and provenance preflight. `review` also runs actual strict change and all-spec validation, verifies the current shared pointer and every declared bundle file against the approved raw bundle hash before loading executable release code, freezes the candidate, invokes the shared physical PRE or POST runner in a dedicated child, retains raw material, and checks the complete event stream and final report. The child inherits `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` and scoped Git configuration while the parent binds the raw index before and after. A focused task diagnostic sets `focused: true`; its PASS is retained as scoped evidence and `closureAuthorized` remains false. Formal Verify is a separate phase and is never called POST. A valid review FAIL stops the owning scope. Codex raw exit 0 means clean transport for PASS and FAIL; the wrapper CLI exits 0, 1, or 2 for PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED. Unavailable runtime, changed source or invalid reception is BLOCKED.
+
+Strict validation discovers the installed public `@fission-ai/openspec` 1.14.0 package from the owner local package or an npm shim directory on `PATH`. +# Direction checkpoint and publication
+
+Use the canonical public CLI after the review freeze is released:
+
+```text
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs checkpoint <absolute-direction.json> <absolute-event.json>
+node scripts/directions/cli.mjs publish <absolute-checkpoint-receipt.json>
+```
+
+The event file is an input record, not an approval. It has `kind` (`TASK`, `PLANNING`, `GATE`, `STAGE`, or `BLOCKER`), `health`, `message`, exact `paths`, and nonempty `evidence` entries containing `path` and raw SHA256. A task event also has its task ID. Include the tracked status path and new raw evidence. A blocker must say `FAIL` or `BLOCKED` in the status and evidence. A receipt alone cannot cause a checkpoint.
+
+The controller provisions `<git-common>/frade-workflow/publication-authority/<direction-id>.json` outside the owner request. Schema version 1 binds the manifest owner, immutable `originalBaseline`, `approvedSourceCommit`, exact `remote` and feature `ref`, `requiredChecks` (unique check IDs), and separate `approval` and `plan` objects with repository paths and SHA256. The approved source commit must descend from the original baseline and precede the current HEAD. The raw D02 decision at that commit must contain the exact approved remote/ref and direct reply. The approved plan must contain the same target and checkpoint cadence; current source bytes must still match. The owner manifest's publication flags and the event's destination strings grant no authority.
+
+For `TASK` and `BLOCKER`, the controller also provisions `<git-common>/frade-workflow/publication-admission/<direction-id>/<event-sha256>.json`. Schema version 1 contains `id`, `kind`, `task` (task ID for `TASK`, `null` for `BLOCKER`), `sourceHead`, `manifestSha256`, `authoritySha256`, `eventSha256`, `candidateSha256`, and `checks`. `candidateSha256` is SHA256 of the concatenation of each sorted event path, NUL, SHA256 of its current raw bytes, and LF. Each check has an authorized `id`, actual `argv`, raw process `exitCode`, `result` (`PASS` or `FAIL`), and `raw: { name: "<id>.log", sha256 }`. The controller writes the actual unmodified check output with its command and exit record under `<git-common>/frade-workflow/publication-checks/<direction-id>/<id>.log`, then binds the log bytes in the admission. These records must be produced from current mandatory native checks for the exact source and candidate before checkpoint. An owner event or owner evidence JSON that says PASS cannot provision admission. A task needs all authorized checks with exit 0 and PASS; FAIL or BLOCKED task health is rejected. A blocker needs at least one actual failed check with raw failure and blocked status, and cannot grant tested-task cadence, GREEN, Verify, or closure. Formal Verify and POST are separate later barriers, not prerequisites for publishing a completed tested implementation task.
+
+Checkpoint checks the registered owning branch/common, freeze lock, scope, every worktree and index path, raw evidence hashes, secret patterns and nonempty new evidence before exact pathspec staging. It validates the actual `origin` fetch and push URLs, exact branch upstream, and absence of repository-local URL rewrites before remote operations. It preserves unrelated files and rejects an occupied index. The result is `CHECKPOINTED`, with the commit SHA and an immutable receipt under Git common storage. It does not assert GREEN, Verify, POST, closure or remote publication.
+
+The default public CLI is bound to Frade's canonical Git common (`E:/dev/codex/frade/.git` on Windows, `/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git` in WSL) and also checks the module's registered worktree/common before reading owner authority or admission. The manifest, event, receipt, current directory, and environment cannot select another control root. A copied CLI in a foreign checkout with matching-looking authority and admission JSON is rejected. Path checks resolve the owner root and each descendant with the platform path rules, reject traversal and sibling roots, and check each existing component's canonical path to reject symbolic links and Windows reparse paths. Disposable bare-remote positives call the copied module API with `trustedPublicationFixtureContext(common, { brand: 'FRADE_PUBLICATION_TEST_CONTROLLER_V1' })` and pass the returned `trustedContext` to `checkpoint` or `publish`; the public CLI does not accept that context. Native childprocess tests cover public CLI rejection for both the original and copied foreign entry. The owning controller separately verifies the installed CLI on the authorized W01 owner.
+
+Publish requires the exact local checkpoint SHA at HEAD. It queries the authorized remote feature ref, checks ancestry, pushes `<checkpoint-SHA>:<exact-ref>` once without force, then independently queries the remote again. Only an exact fresh SHA match produces `PUBLISHED`. Failed push, unavailable transport, divergence and mismatched SHA remain `BLOCKED` with local work retained. The publication receipt stores raw Git argv, status, signal, reported spawn error, exit code and output outside the candidate. A reported spawn error or signal blocks publication even if the process status is zero; no synthetic exit code replaces the raw status. A second publish attempt for the same SHA is refused. Recovery keeps the blocked receipt and its failed commands, diagnoses the transport or remote mismatch, and creates a new coherent checkpoint with new status/evidence and fresh controller admission. Its new SHA can be published once after the destination is corrected; a successful push discovered after a post-push mismatch still requires an explicit new checkpoint rather than a hidden retry or a false PUBLISHED claim.
+
+After publication, refresh the tracked status at the next natural task, plan, gate, stage or blocker checkpoint. Copy the prior immutable publication receipt into scoped evidence, set `previousPublicationReceipt` to the prior checkpoint SHA, and record both prior source and verified remote SHA in status. The receipt joins that next checkpoint; it never triggers a receipt-only commit. Formal Verify, current independent POST and closure barriers remain separate.
+
+For W01 the production target is `git@github.com:leonmaks/frade.git` at `refs/heads/codex/frade-standard-workflow` only. This worker's tests use disposable local bare remotes. The actual production authority record and live GitHub invocation belong to the owning controller.

+  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: process.platform === 'win32' ? 'NUL' : '/dev/null',
+  GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS: '0',

+  '-c',

+async function verifyOwner(r, plan, { allowProgress = false } = {}) {

+async function ensureParents(root, path) {

+async function writeSeed(root, data, baselineAgents) {

+export async function planDirection(request, options = {}) {

+      plan.targetExists &&

+export async function checkDirection(manifestPath, options = {}) {

+      !samePath(control.common, m.owner.gitCommon) ||

+      control.policySha256 !== m.policy.sha256 ||
+      control.policyVersion !== m.policy.version

+      m.owner.worktree,
+      git(m.owner.worktree, ['rev-parse', '--git-common-dir']),
+    )

+      !samePath(common, m.owner.gitCommon) ||

+    )

+    if (git(m.owner.worktree, ['cat-file', '-t', m.originalBaseline]) !== 'commit')

+    if (
+      spawnSync('git', [...gitOptions, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', m.originalBaseline, head], {
+        cwd: m.owner.worktree,

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
+import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
+import { resolve } from 'node:path'
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
+import { safeId } from './contracts.mjs'
+
+const protectedPaths = [
+  'packages',
+  'apps',
+  'pnpm-lock.yaml',
+  'docs/routing-v2',
+  'vendor',
+  'scripts/routing-v2-architecture-gate.mjs',
+]
+const sha256 = (bytes) => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex')
+const blocked = (detail) => ({
+  ok: false,
+  status: 'BLOCKED',
+  code: 'APPLICABILITY',
+  detail,
+  productChecks: 'NOT_RUN',
+})
+function git(root, ...args) {
+  const run = spawnSync(
+    'git',
+    ['-c', 'core.fsmonitor=false', '-c', 'core.useBuiltinFSMonitor=false', ...args],
+    { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' },
+  )
+  if (run.error || run.signal || run.status !== 0)
+    throw new Error(
+      `git ${args.join(' ')}: status=${run.status} signal=${run.signal} error=${run.error?.code ?? 'none'} stderr=${run.stderr?.trim() ?? ''}`,
+    )
+  return run.stdout.trim()
+}
+
+export function checkApplicability({ root } = {}) {
+  try {
+    root = resolve(root)
+    const planBytes = readFileSync(resolve(root, 'docs/engineering/check-applicability.json'))
+    const plan = JSON.parse(planBytes)
+    if (
+      plan.version !== 1 ||
+      !safeId(plan.owner) ||
+      plan.decidedBeforeExecution !== true ||
+      !/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(plan.baseline)
+    )
+      throw new Error('INVALID_APPLICABILITY_PLAN')
+    if (
+      !Array.isArray(plan.required) ||
+      !plan.required.includes('direction-controls') ||
+      !Array.isArray(plan.notApplicable) ||
+      plan.notApplicable.some((x) => !x.family || !x.reason)
+    )
+      throw new Error('INCOMPLETE_APPLICABILITY_PLAN')
+    const manifest = JSON.parse(
+      readFileSync(
+        resolve(root, `docs/engineering/directions/${plan.owner}/direction.json`),
+        'utf8',
+      ),
+    )
+    if (manifest.id !== plan.owner || manifest.originalBaseline !== plan.baseline)
+      throw new Error('BASELINE_MISMATCH')
+    if (
+      plan.owner === 'frade-standard-workflow' &&
+      plan.baseline !== '98f387f96b51b0ad139e3507c376ff1c3e8dec09'
+    )
+      throw new Error('W01_BASELINE_DRIFT')
+    git(root, 'cat-file', '-e', `${plan.baseline}^{commit}`)
+    const committed = git(
+      root,
+      'diff',
+      '--name-only',
+      plan.baseline,
+      'HEAD',
+      '--',
+      ...protectedPaths,
+    )
+    const working = git(
+      root,
+      'status',
+      '--porcelain=v1',
+      '--untracked-files=all',
+      '--',
+      ...protectedPaths,
+    )
+    if (committed || working)
+      throw new Error(`PROTECTED_TREE_CHANGED committed=${committed} working=${working}`)
+    const tree = git(root, 'ls-tree', '-r', 'HEAD', '--', ...protectedPaths)
+    return {
+      ok: true,
+      status: 'APPLICABILITY_PROVEN',
+      baseline: plan.baseline,
+      sourceHead: git(root, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'),
+      planSha256: sha256(planBytes),
+      protectedTreeSha256: sha256(tree),
+      protectedPaths,
+      notApplicable: plan.notApplicable.map((x) => x.family),
+      productChecks: 'NOT_RUN',
+    }
+  } catch (error) {
+    return blocked(error.message)
+  }
+}
+
+if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
+  const root = resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL('../..', import.meta.url)))
+  const result = checkApplicability({ root })
+  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(result)}\n`)
+  if (!result.ok) process.exitCode = 2
+}

+    )
+      owners = scenarioOwners(finding.path)
+    else if (finding.code === 'TRACE_TASK_SCENARIO') owners = taskOwners(finding.path)
+    else if (finding.code === 'TRACE_RUN') owners = assertionOwners(finding.path)
+    else if (finding.code === 'RUN_BINDING') owners = runOwners(finding.path)
+    if (!owners.length || owners.some((id) => requirements.filter((r) => r.id === id).length !== 1))
+      unassignable = true
+    else owners.forEach((id) => blocked.add(id))
+  }
+  if (unassignable) return 0
+  return requirements.filter((r) => {
+    if (
+      blocked.has(r.id) ||
+      r.unresolved?.length ||
+      !/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)+$/.test(r.id) ||
+      r.id.length > 80 ||
+      requirements.filter((other) => other.id === r.id).length !== 1 ||
+      !Array.isArray(r.scenarioIds) ||
+      !r.scenarioIds.length ||
+      new Set(r.scenarioIds).size !== r.scenarioIds.length
+    )
+      return false
+    const linked = scenarios.filter((s) => s.requirementId === r.id)
+    if (
+      linked.length !== r.scenarioIds.length ||
+      !r.scenarioIds.every((id) => linked.filter((s) => s.id === id).length === 1) ||
+      (r.critical &&
+        ['positive', 'negative', 'boundary'].some(
+          (control) => !linked.some((s) => s.control === control),
+        ))
+    )
+      return false
+    return linked.every((s) => {
+      if (
+        !['positive', 'negative', 'boundary'].includes(s.control) ||
+        !proven.has(s.id) ||
+        !Array.isArray(s.taskIds) ||
+        !s.taskIds.length ||
+        new Set(s.taskIds).size !== s.taskIds.length ||
+        !s.taskIds.every((id) => {
+          const matching = tasks.filter((task) => task.id === id)
+          return (
+            matching.length === 1 &&
+            Array.isArray(matching[0].scenarioIds) &&
+            matching[0].scenarioIds.includes(s.id)
+          )
+        }) ||
+        tasks.some(
+          (task) =>
+            Array.isArray(task.scenarioIds) &&
+            task.scenarioIds.includes(s.id) &&
+            !s.taskIds.includes(task.id),
+        ) ||
+        !Array.isArray(s.assertionIds) ||
+        !s.assertionIds.length ||
+        new Set(s.assertionIds).size !== s.assertionIds.length
+      )
+        return false
+      return s.assertionIds.every((id) => {
+        const matching = assertions.filter((a) => a.id === id)
+        return (
+          matching.length === 1 &&
+          runs.filter((run) => run.id === matching[0].runId).length === 1 &&
+          runProof.get(matching[0].runId) === true
+        )
+      })
+    })
+  }).length
+}
+
+export async function verifyTraceability(
+  trace,
+  { boundary, snapshot, action = 'IMPLEMENTATION' } = {},
+) {
+  const issues = [...validateTraceability(trace, { action }).issues]
+  const { verifyGate } = await import('./evidence.mjs')
+  if (!hash64(snapshot?.sourceSha256) || !hash64(snapshot?.configSha256))
+    add(issues, 'TRACE_SNAPSHOT', 'snapshot', 'Current source/config hashes required')
+  const referenced = new Set(
+    (Array.isArray(trace?.assertions) ? trace.assertions : []).map((a) => a?.runId),
+  )
+  for (const run of (Array.isArray(trace?.runs) ? trace.runs : []).filter((r) =>
+    referenced.has(r?.id),
+  )) {
+    if (
+      run?.status !== 'PASS' ||
+      run?.sourceSha256 !== snapshot?.sourceSha256 ||
+      run?.configSha256 !== snapshot?.configSha256 ||
+      !(await verifyGate(boundary, 'run', run, {
+        sourceSha256: snapshot?.sourceSha256,
+        configSha256: snapshot?.configSha256,
+      }))
+    )
+      add(issues, 'TRACE_RUN_PROOF', run?.id, 'Current trusted raw run proof required')
+  }
+  return outcome(issues)
+}
+
+export function validateApplicability(plan = {}) {
+  if (!obj(plan))
+    return outcome([{ code: 'APPLICABILITY_SHAPE', path: '$', detail: 'Plan object required' }])
+  const { checks, affectedContracts = [], previousResults = [] } = plan
+  const issues = []
+  if (
+    !Array.isArray(checks) ||
+    !Array.isArray(affectedContracts) ||
+    !Array.isArray(previousResults)
+  )
+    return outcome([{ code: 'APPLICABILITY_SHAPE', path: '$', detail: 'Arrays required' }])
+  for (const c of checks) {
+    if (!APPLICABILITY.includes(c?.applicability))
+      add(issues, 'APPLICABILITY', c?.id, 'Unknown applicability')
+    if (c?.applicability === 'NOT_APPLICABLE') {
+      if (
+        affectedContracts.includes(c.contract) ||
+        previousResults.some((r) => r?.id === c.id && r?.status === 'FAIL')
+      )
+        add(issues, 'FALSE_NOT_APPLICABLE', c.id, 'Affected or failing check cannot be waived')
+      if (typeof c.reason !== 'string' || c.reason.trim().length < 20)
+        add(issues, 'NA_REASON', c.id, 'Contract reason required')
+    }
+    if (c?.applicability === 'REQUIRED' && c.status !== 'PASS')
+      add(issues, 'REQUIRED_CHECK_NOT_PASS', c.id, 'Required run not passing')
+  }
+  return outcome(issues)
+}
+
+export async function verifyApplicability(plan, options = {}) {
+  const validation = validateApplicability(plan)
+  if (!validation.ok) return validation
+  if (!obj(options))
+    return outcome([
+      { code: 'APPLICABILITY_OPTIONS_SHAPE', path: '$', detail: 'Options object required' },
+    ])
+  const { boundary, snapshot } = options
+  const issues = []
+  const { verifyGate } = await import('./evidence.mjs')
+  if (!hash64(snapshot?.sourceSha256) || !hash64(snapshot?.configSha256))
+    add(issues, 'CHECK_SNAPSHOT', 'snapshot', 'Current source/config hashes required')
+  for (const c of Array.isArray(plan?.checks) ? plan.checks : [])
+    if (
+      c?.applicability === 'REQUIRED' &&
+      !(await verifyGate(boundary, 'check', c, {
+        sourceSha256: snapshot?.sourceSha256,
+        configSha256: snapshot?.configSha256,
+      }))
+    )
+      add(issues, 'CHECK_PROOF', c?.id, 'Current trusted raw check run required')
+  return outcome(issues)
+}

+import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
+import { lstat, readFile, realpath } from 'node:fs/promises'
+import { resolve, sep } from 'node:path'
+import { safeRepoPath } from './contracts.mjs'
+
+const boundaries = new WeakSet()
+
+// The root is chosen by a trusted caller. Every component is checked before the file is read.
+export function createArtifactReader(root) {
+  if (typeof root !== 'string' || !root) throw new TypeError('Artifact root required')
+  const base = resolve(root)
+  const within = (path) =>
+    process.platform === 'win32'
+      ? path.toLowerCase().startsWith(`${base}${sep}`.toLowerCase())
+      : path.startsWith(`${base}${sep}`)
+  return Object.freeze({
+    async read(path) {
+      if (!safeRepoPath(path)) throw new Error('UNSAFE_ARTIFACT: unsafe relative path')
+      let cursor = base
+      for (const part of path.split('/')) {
+        cursor = resolve(cursor, part)
+        if (!within(cursor)) throw new Error('UNSAFE_ARTIFACT: outside root')
+        const stat = await lstat(cursor)
+        if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error('UNSAFE_ARTIFACT: symlink')
+      }
+      const canonical = await realpath(cursor)
+      if (!within(canonical)) throw new Error('UNSAFE_ARTIFACT: realpath escape')
+      const bytes = await readFile(cursor)
+      return Object.freeze({
+        path,
+        bytes,
+        sha256: createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex'),
+      })
+    },
+  })
+}
+
+// Only a trusted integration supplies verify: it must inspect actual raw artifacts, hashes,
+// complete execution, independent receipt, scope and bindings. No JSON field is an authority.
+export function createEvidenceBoundary({ verify } = {}) {
+  if (typeof verify !== 'function') throw new TypeError('Trusted evidence verifier required')
+  const boundary = Object.freeze({ verify: (kind, ref, expected) => verify(kind, ref, expected) })
+  boundaries.add(boundary)
+  return boundary
+}
+
+export const isEvidenceBoundary = (x) => boundaries.has(x)
+
+export async function verifyArtifactHash(reader, descriptor) {
+  if (
+    typeof reader?.read !== 'function' ||
+    !safeRepoPath(descriptor?.path) ||
+    !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(descriptor?.sha256 ?? '')
+  )
+    return false
+  try {
+    return (await reader.read(descriptor.path)).sha256 === descriptor.sha256
+  } catch {
+    return false
+  }
+}
+
+export async function verifyGate(boundary, kind, ref, expected) {
+  if (
+    !isEvidenceBoundary(boundary) ||
+    !ref ||
+    typeof ref !== 'object' ||
+    Array.isArray(ref) ||
+    ref.kind !== kind ||
+    ref.status !== 'PASS' ||
+    ref.complete !== true ||
+    ref.scope !== 'full' ||
+    !safeRepoPath(ref.artifact?.path) ||
+    !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(ref.artifact?.sha256 ?? '') ||
+    !ref.bindings ||
+    typeof ref.bindings !== 'object' ||
+    Object.entries(expected).some(([k, v]) => ref.bindings[k] !== v)
+  )
+    return false
+  try {
+    return (await boundary.verify(kind, ref, expected)) === true
+  } catch {
+    return false
+  }
+}

+import { PHASES, scopeFingerprint, validateManifest } from './contracts.mjs'
+import { isEvidenceBoundary, verifyGate } from './evidence.mjs'
+import { isClosureReceipt } from './scope.mjs'
+
+const issue = (issues, code, path, detail) => issues.push({ code, path, detail })
+const hash = (x) => typeof x === 'string' && /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(x)
+const EXPECTED = {
+  policyDecision: (s) => ({ planSha256: s.planSha256, scopeSha256: s.scopeSha256 }),
+  checkpoint: (s) => ({ planSha256: s.planSha256, scopeSha256: s.scopeSha256 }),
+  pre: (s) => ({ planSha256: s.planSha256, scopeSha256: s.scopeSha256 }),
+  red: (s) => ({ planSha256: s.planSha256, scopeSha256: s.scopeSha256 }),
+  green: (s) => ({ sourceSha256: s.sourceSha256, configSha256: s.configSha256 }),
+  checks: (s) => ({ sourceSha256: s.sourceSha256, configSha256: s.configSha256 }),
+  verify: (s) => ({ sourceSha256: s.sourceSha256, configSha256: s.configSha256 }),
+  post: (s) => ({
+    sourceSha256: s.sourceSha256,
+    configSha256: s.configSha256,
+    planSha256: s.planSha256,
+    scopeSha256: s.scopeSha256,
+  }),
+}
+const CODE = {
+  policyDecision: 'POLICY_DECISION_PROOF',
+  checkpoint: 'CHECKPOINT_PROOF',
+  pre: 'PRE_PROOF',
+  red: 'RED_PROOF',
+  green: 'GREEN_PROOF',
+  checks: 'CHECKS_PROOF',
+  verify: 'VERIFY_PROOF',
+  post: 'POST_PROOF',
+}
+const NEED = {
+  PRE_REVIEW: ['policyDecision', 'checkpoint'],
+  BDD_TDD: ['policyDecision', 'checkpoint', 'pre'],
+  IMPLEMENTATION: ['policyDecision', 'checkpoint', 'pre', 'red'],
+  CHECKS: ['policyDecision', 'checkpoint', 'pre', 'red'],
+  VERIFICATION: ['policyDecision', 'checkpoint', 'pre', 'red', 'green', 'checks'],
+  POST_REVIEW: ['policyDecision', 'checkpoint', 'pre', 'red', 'green', 'checks', 'verify'],
+  ARCHIVE: ['policyDecision', 'checkpoint', 'pre', 'red', 'green', 'checks', 'verify', 'post'],
+  CLOSED: ['policyDecision', 'checkpoint', 'pre', 'red', 'green', 'checks', 'verify', 'post'],
+}
+const RCA_CLASSES = new Set([
+  'DOMAIN_MODEL',
+  'INVARIANT',
+  'ALGORITHM',
+  'ABSTRACTION_BOUNDARY',
+  'STATE_TRANSITION',
+  'TEST',
+  'SPEC_CONFLICT',
+  'INTEGRATION',
+  'ENVIRONMENT',
+])
+
+export async function evaluateTransition(options = {}) {
+  if (options === null || typeof options !== 'object' || Array.isArray(options))
+    return {
+      ok: false,
+      issues: [{ code: 'TRANSITION_SHAPE', path: '$', detail: 'Options object required' }],
+    }
+  const { manifest, stageId, target, evidence = {}, boundary, snapshot } = options
+  const issues = [...validateManifest(manifest).issues]
+  const stage = Array.isArray(manifest?.stages)
+    ? manifest.stages.find((s) => s?.id === stageId)
+    : undefined
+  if (!stage) issue(issues, 'STAGE_UNKNOWN', 'stageId', 'Stage absent')
+  if (!PHASES.includes(target)) issue(issues, 'PHASE', 'target', 'Unknown target phase')
+  if (
+    stage &&
+    PHASES.includes(target) &&
+    PHASES.indexOf(target) !== PHASES.indexOf(stage.phase) + 1
+  )
+    issue(issues, 'PHASE_ORDER', 'target', 'Only the next phase can be entered')
+  if (stage && ['FAIL', 'BLOCKED', 'PAUSED'].includes(stage.health))
+    issue(issues, 'HEALTH_STOP', 'stage.health', 'Owner stop state')
+  if (
+    !snapshot ||
+    !['planSha256', 'scopeSha256', 'sourceSha256', 'configSha256'].every((k) => hash(snapshot[k]))
+  )
+    issue(
+      issues,
+      'SNAPSHOT_BINDING',
+      'snapshot',
+      'Current raw plan/scope/source/config hashes required',
+    )
+  if (!issues.length && snapshot.scopeSha256 !== scopeFingerprint(manifest))
+    issue(
+      issues,
+      'SCOPE_DRIFT',
+      'snapshot.scopeSha256',
+      'Snapshot does not bind current semantic scope',
+    )
+  if (!isEvidenceBoundary(boundary))
+    issue(issues, 'EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY', 'boundary', 'Trusted verifier required')
+  if (
+    issues.some((x) => ['MANIFEST_SHAPE', 'SNAPSHOT_BINDING', 'EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY'].includes(x.code))
+  )
+    return { ok: false, issues }
+  for (const kind of NEED[target] ?? [])
+    if (!(await verifyGate(boundary, kind, evidence?.[kind], EXPECTED[kind](snapshot))))
+      issue(issues, CODE[kind], `evidence.${kind}`, 'Missing, stale or unverified gate proof')
+  if (target === 'IMPLEMENTATION' && stage) {
+    const failures = Array.isArray(stage.failedFixes) ? stage.failedFixes : []
+    const counts = new Map()
+    for (const f of failures)
+      if (
+        f?.deterministic === true &&
+        f?.status === 'FAIL' &&
+        typeof f?.defectId === 'string' &&
+        f.defectId
+      )
+        counts.set(f.defectId, (counts.get(f.defectId) ?? 0) + 1)
+    for (const [defectId, count] of counts)
+      if (count >= 2) {
+        const rca = stage.rca
+        if (
+          rca?.defectId !== defectId ||
+          !RCA_CLASSES.has(rca?.classification) ||
+          typeof rca?.root !== 'string' ||
+          rca.root.trim().length < 10 ||
+          typeof rca?.layer !== 'string' ||
+          rca.layer.trim().length < 3
+        )
+          issue(
+            issues,
+            'RCA_REQUIRED',
+            'stage.rca',
+            'Classified root and responsible layer required after two failed fixes',
+          )
+        else if (
+          rca?.artifact?.path !== evidence?.rca?.artifact?.path ||
+          rca?.artifact?.sha256 !== evidence?.rca?.artifact?.sha256 ||
+          !(await verifyGate(boundary, 'rca', evidence?.rca, {
+            planSha256: snapshot.planSha256,
+            scopeSha256: snapshot.scopeSha256,
+            defectId,
+            classification: rca.classification,
+            root: rca.root,
+            layer: rca.layer,
+          }))
+        )
+          issue(
+            issues,
+            'RCA_PROOF',
+            'evidence.rca',
+            'Trusted classified RCA proof bound to documented source required',
+          )
+      }
+  }
+  if (target === 'CLOSED') {
+    const receipt = evidence?.closureReceipt
+    const publication = evidence?.archive?.bindings
+    if (
+      !/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(publication?.checkpointSha ?? '') ||
+      publication?.publishedSha !== publication?.checkpointSha ||
+      publication?.publicationRef !== `refs/heads/${manifest?.owner?.branch}`
+    )
+      issue(
+        issues,
+        'ARCHIVE_PUBLICATION',
+        'evidence.archive.bindings',
+        'Bound checkpoint SHA and verified authorized publication required',
+      )
+    if (
+      !isClosureReceipt(receipt, { manifest, stageId, snapshot }) ||
+      !(await verifyGate(boundary, 'archive', evidence?.archive, {
+        planSha256: snapshot.planSha256,
+        scopeSha256: snapshot.scopeSha256,
+        sourceSha256: snapshot.sourceSha256,
+        configSha256: snapshot.configSha256,
+        archiveHead: receipt?.head,
+        archive: receipt?.archive,
+        operationSha256: receipt?.operationSha256,
+        publicationRef: `refs/heads/${manifest.owner.branch}`,
+      }))
+    )
+      issue(
+        issues,
+        'ARCHIVE_PROOF',
+        'evidence.archive',
+        'Actual owner archive, checkpoint and publication authority required',
+      )
+  }
+  return { ok: issues.length === 0, issues }
+}
+
+// Historical labels are only a conservative projection. Even all textual PASS fields
+// do not establish independent review or archive proof.
+export function legacyClosureState(record = {}) {
+  return record.tasksComplete === true ? 'IMPLEMENTED_PENDING_CLOSURE' : 'IN_PROGRESS'
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env node

+import { safeRepoPath, pathMatches, validateManifest } from './contracts.mjs'

+const sha = (bytes) => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex')
+const hash40 = (x) => typeof x === 'string' && /^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(x)
+const hash64 = (x) => typeof x === 'string' && /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(x)

+  ok: false,
+  status: 'BLOCKED',
+  code,
+  detail,
+  ...more,
+})
+const productionCommon =
+  process.platform === 'win32' ? 'E:/dev/codex/frade/.git' : '/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git'

+    throw Error('FIXTURE_CONTROLLER_REQUIRED')

+  plainDirectory(canonical)
+  const context = Object.freeze({ common: canonical })

+}
+const env = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter(([k]) => !k.startsWith('GIT_')))
+env.GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM = '1'
+env.GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL = process.platform === 'win32' ? 'NUL' : '/dev/null'
+env.GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT = '0'
+env.GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS = '0'
+const gitPrefix = [
+  '-c',
+  'core.autocrlf=false',
+  '-c',
+  'core.hooksPath=/dev/null',
+  '-c',
+  'core.fsmonitor=false',
+  '-c',
+  'core.attributesFile=/dev/null',
+  '-c',
+  'core.sshCommand=ssh',
+  '-c',
+  'credential.helper=',
+  '-c',
+  'protocol.ext.allow=never',
+]
+export function checkedGitRecord(args, run, commands) {
+  const record = {
+    args,
+    exitCode: run.status,
+    status: run.status,
+    signal: run.signal ?? null,
+    stdout: run.stdout ?? '',
+    stderr: run.stderr ?? '',
+    error: run.error?.message ?? null,

+function git(cwd, args, commands) {

+    cwd,

+    maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
+  })

+}
+function need(cwd, args, commands) {

+function plainFile(path) {

+}

+}
+function inScope(m, path) {
+  return (
+    safeRepoPath(path) &&
+    m.scope.allowed.some((pattern) => pathMatches(pattern, path)) &&
+    !m.scope.frozen.some((pattern) => pathMatches(pattern, path)) &&
+    !(

+      ok: true,
+      status: match[1],

+    return blocked(error.message || 'REVIEW_RAW')
+  }
+}

+      metadata.version !== publicOpenSpecVersion ||
+      metadata.bin?.openspec !== './bin/openspec.js'
+    )

+      node,
+      nodeSha256: sha(await readFile(node)),

+async function materializePacket(owner, prepared, run) {

+      throw Error('REVIEW_SOURCE_DRIFT')

+    await mkdir(dirname(dest), { recursive: true })
+    await writeFile(dest, bytes, { flag: 'wx' })

+    flag: 'wx',
+  })

+      throw Error('REVIEW_PACKET_DRIFT')

+export async function captureSharedRaw(common, sharedRun, run, testPin) {
+  const expectedTarget = testPin === undefined ? RUNTIME_BINARY : rawCaptureTestPins.get(testPin)
+  if (!expectedTarget) throw Error('REVIEW_TEST_PIN')
+  const root = join(common, 'frade-workflow', 'runs')
+  if (!inside(root, sharedRun) || !samePath(await realpath(sharedRun), sharedRun))
+    throw Error('REVIEW_SHARED_RUN_PATH')
+  const target = join(run, 'shared-raw')
+  await mkdir(target)
+  const artifacts = []
+  const exclusions = []
+  const seen = new Set()
+  const walk = async (relativePath = '') => {
+    const current = join(sharedRun, relativePath)
+    await safeDirectory(current)
+    for (const entry of await readdir(current, { withFileTypes: true })) {
+      const child = relativePath ? `${relativePath}/${entry.name}` : entry.name
+      const origin = join(sharedRun, child)
+      if (!safeRepoPath(child) || seen.has(child.toLowerCase()))
+        throw Error('REVIEW_SHARED_RUN_PATH')
+      seen.add(child.toLowerCase())
+      const state = await lstat(origin)
+      if (state.isSymbolicLink() || !samePath(await realpath(origin), origin)) {
+        const match = /^offline-home\/tmp\/arg0\/(codex-arg0[A-Za-z0-9]{6})\/([^/]+)$/.exec(child)
+        if (
+          !state.isSymbolicLink() ||
+          !match ||
+          !RUNTIME_LINKS.has(match[2]) ||
+          !linkTargetMatches(await readlink(origin), expectedTarget, testPin) ||
+          exclusions.length >= 4
+        )
+          throw Error('REVIEW_SHARED_RUN_LINK')
+        exclusions.push({
+          path: child,
+          kind: 'runtime-symlink',
+          target: await readlink(origin),
+          reason: 'Codex canary offline home; outside reviewer evidence',
+        })
+      } else if (state.isDirectory()) {
+        await mkdir(join(target, child))
+        await walk(child)
+      } else if (state.isFile()) {
+        const bytes = await readRegularNoFollow(origin)
+        const copy = join(target, child)
+        await writeFile(copy, bytes, { flag: 'wx' })
+        if (
+          sha(await readRegularNoFollow(copy)) !== sha(bytes) ||
+          sha(await readRegularNoFollow(origin)) !== sha(bytes)
+        )
+          throw Error('REVIEW_SHARED_RAW_DRIFT')
+        artifacts.push({
+          path: child,
+          bytes: bytes.length,
+          sha256: sha(bytes),
+        })
+      } else throw Error('REVIEW_SHARED_RUN_TYPE')
+    }
+  }
+  await walk()
+  if (exclusions.length !== 4 || new Set(exclusions.map((x) => dirname(x.path))).size !== 1)
+    throw Error('REVIEW_SHARED_RUN_LINK')
+  const afterPaths = []
+  const inventory = async (relativePath = '') => {
+    const directory = join(sharedRun, relativePath)
+    await safeDirectory(directory)
+    for (const entry of await readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true })) {
+      const child = relativePath ? `${relativePath}/${entry.name}` : entry.name
+      afterPaths.push(child.toLowerCase())
+      const state = await lstat(join(sharedRun, child))
+      if (state.isDirectory() && !state.isSymbolicLink()) await inventory(child)
+    }
+  }
+  await inventory()
+  if (JSON.stringify(afterPaths.sort()) !== JSON.stringify([...seen].sort()))
+    throw Error('REVIEW_SHARED_RAW_DRIFT')
+  artifacts.sort((a, b) => a.path.localeCompare(b.path))
+  for (const artifact of artifacts) {
+    const source = await readRegularNoFollow(join(sharedRun, artifact.path))
+    const copy = await readRegularNoFollow(join(target, artifact.path))
+    if (
+      source.length !== artifact.bytes ||
+      copy.length !== artifact.bytes ||
+      sha(source) !== artifact.sha256 ||
+      sha(copy) !== artifact.sha256
+    )
+      throw Error('REVIEW_SHARED_RAW_DRIFT')
+  }
+  for (const excluded of exclusions) {
+    const path = join(sharedRun, excluded.path)
+    if (!(await lstat(path)).isSymbolicLink() || (await readlink(path)) !== excluded.target)
+      throw Error('REVIEW_SHARED_RAW_DRIFT')
+  }
+  await writeFile(join(run, 'shared-raw-index.json'), JSON.stringify(artifacts, null, 2) + '\n', {
+    flag: 'wx',
+  })
+  await writeFile(
+    join(run, 'shared-runtime-exclusions.json'),
+    JSON.stringify(
+      {
+        max: 4,
+        allowedPath: 'offline-home/tmp/arg0/codex-arg0<six-alphanumeric>/<named-utility>',
+        expectedTarget,
+        exclusions,
+      },
+      null,
+      2,
+    ) + '\n',
+    { flag: 'wx' },
+  )
+  return {
+    root: target,
+    sourceRun: sharedRun,
+    artifacts,
+    exclusions,
+    digest: sha(JSON.stringify({ artifacts, exclusions })),
+  }
+}
+
+async function retainedRawComplete(run, raw, captured) {
+  if (!raw || !captured || !Array.isArray(captured.artifacts) || captured.artifacts.length === 0)
+    return false
+  const names = {
+    events: 'events.jsonl',
+    report: 'result.md',
+    stderr: 'stderr.txt',
+    exit: 'exit.json',
+  }
+  for (const [key, name] of Object.entries(names)) {
+    const descriptor = raw[key]
+    if (
+      !descriptor ||
+      !samePath(descriptor.path, join(run, name)) ||
+      !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(descriptor.sha256)
+    )
+      return false
+    const bytes = await readRegularNoFollow(descriptor.path)
+    if (bytes.length !== descriptor.bytes || sha(bytes) !== descriptor.sha256) return false
+  }
+  const rawExit = JSON.parse(await readRegularNoFollow(raw.exit.path))
+  if (rawExit.exit !== 0 || rawExit.timedOut !== false) return false
+  const verified = verifyRawReview({
+    events: (await readRegularNoFollow(raw.events.path)).toString('utf8'),
+    report: (await readRegularNoFollow(raw.report.path)).toString('utf8'),
+    exit: rawExit.exit,
+  })
+  if (!verified.ok) return false
+  for (const [key, name] of [
+    ['events', 'events.jsonl'],
+    ['report', 'result.md'],
+    ['stderr', 'stderr.txt'],
+  ]) {
+    if (sha(await readRegularNoFollow(join(captured.root, 'output', name))) !== raw[key].sha256)
+      return false
+  }
+  const sharedRecord = JSON.parse(
+    await readRegularNoFollow(join(captured.root, 'output', 'record.json')),
+  )
+  const sharedReceipt = JSON.parse(await readRegularNoFollow(join(captured.root, 'receipt.json')))
+  if (
+    sharedRecord.exitCode !== rawExit.exit ||
+    sharedRecord.timedOut === true ||
+    sharedRecord.candidateUnchanged !== true ||
+    sharedRecord.packetUnchanged !== true ||
+    sharedRecord.error ||
+    !['PASS', 'FAIL'].includes(sharedRecord.status) ||
+    sharedRecord.status !== verified.status ||
+    sharedRecord.gateStatus !== sharedRecord.status ||
+    sharedRecord.resultSha256 !== raw.report.sha256 ||
+    sharedReceipt.status !== sharedRecord.status ||
+    sharedReceipt.resultSha256 !== raw.report.sha256 ||
+    sharedReceipt.candidateUnchanged !== true ||
+    sharedReceipt.packetUnchanged !== true ||
+    sharedReceipt.error
+  )
+    return false
+  const index = JSON.parse(await readRegularNoFollow(join(run, 'shared-raw-index.json')))
+  const metadata = JSON.parse(
+    await readRegularNoFollow(join(run, 'shared-runtime-exclusions.json')),
+  )
+  if (
+    JSON.stringify(index) !== JSON.stringify(captured.artifacts) ||
+    JSON.stringify(metadata.exclusions) !== JSON.stringify(captured.exclusions)
+  )
+    return false
+  if (
+    sha(JSON.stringify({ artifacts: index, exclusions: metadata.exclusions })) !== captured.digest
+  )
+    return false
+  for (const artifact of index) {
+    if (!safeRepoPath(artifact.path) || !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(artifact.sha256)) return false
+    const bytes = await readRegularNoFollow(join(captured.root, artifact.path))
+    if (bytes.length !== artifact.bytes || sha(bytes) !== artifact.sha256) return false
+  }
+  return true
+}
+
+export async function releaseReviewFreeze({
+  lock,
+  run,
+  ownerRoot,
+  snapshotSha256,
+  branch,
+  raw,
+  captured,
+  termination,
+}) {
+  try {
+    if (
+      !terminationProofs.has(termination) ||
+      !termination.stopped ||
+      !captured?.sourceRun ||
+      typeof termination.sharedRun !== 'string' ||
+      !samePath(termination.sharedRun, captured.sourceRun) ||
+      termination.runId !== basename(captured.sourceRun) ||
+      captured.artifacts?.find((artifact) => artifact.path === 'output/record.json')?.sha256 !==
+        termination.recordSha256
+    )
+      return blocked('REVIEW_FREEZE_TERMINATION_OR_BINDING')
+    if (!(await retainedRawComplete(run, raw, captured))) return blocked('REVIEW_RAW_INCOMPLETE')
+    const record = JSON.parse(await readRegularNoFollow(lock))
+    if (
+      !samePath(record.run, run) ||
+      !samePath(record.owner, ownerRoot) ||
+      record.snapshotSha256 !== snapshotSha256 ||
+      record.branch !== branch ||
+      (await snapshotCandidate(ownerRoot)).digest !== snapshotSha256 ||
+      (await ownerIdentity(ownerRoot)).branch !== branch
+    )
+      return blocked('REVIEW_FREEZE_BINDING')
+    await writeFile(join(run, 'termination.json'), JSON.stringify(termination, null, 2) + '\n', {
+      flag: 'wx',
+    })
+    await rm(lock)
+    return { ok: true, status: 'RELEASED' }
+  } catch (error) {
+    return blocked(error.message || 'REVIEW_FREEZE')
+  }
+}

+      raw: descriptors,
+      captured,
+      termination,
+    })
+    return freezeRelease.ok ? wrapper : { ...blocked(freezeRelease.code), run: locked.run }
+  } catch (error) {
+    const result = {
+      ...blocked(error.message || 'REVIEW_RUNTIME'),
+      run: locked?.run,
+      sharedRawIndexSha256: captured?.digest,
+    }
+    if (locked) {
+      try {
+        await writeFile(
+          join(locked.run, 'wrapper-error.json'),
+          JSON.stringify(
+            {
+              error: String(error),
+              atUtc: new Date().toISOString(),
+            },
+            null,
+            2,
+          ) + '\n',
+          { flag: 'wx' },
+        )
+      } catch {
+        /* retain freeze on unavailable owner or failed raw retention */
+      }
+    }

+  }
